key_insight: The paper shows that single-circuit QGAN image generation can be stabilized by calibrating the quantum prior’s fidelity landscape to match the data before adversarial training.
engineering_relevance: This offers a lower-overhead route to end-to-end pixel-level quantum image generation, with fewer qubits and parameters than patch-based QGAN designs.
method: Define the Quantum Fidelity Landscape (QFL) as the pairwise-fidelity structure of a quantum-state ensemble.
Use QFL invariance under shared unitary transformations to relate prior structure to decoded sample separation.
Introduce BasicQGAN, which calibrates the prior-induced QFL to the data-induced QFL before adversarial optimization.
evidence_signal: On small-scale grayscale image datasets, QFL-calibrated BasicQGAN is reported to generate images stably and effectively while using fewer qubits and trainable parameters than representative patch-based quantum generators.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated on small grayscale datasets, so scalability to larger, higher-resolution, or fully practical NISQ settings remains uncertain.
paper_title: Quantum Fidelity Landscape-Guided Prior Calibration for Single-Circuit QGAN Image Generation
